sources.locator: "Mapuche uprising of 1655", revision 1370627596, § Spanish slave hunting

explanation: The uprising's own article puts the two in one sequence and says which way it runs: "In 1654 a large slave-hunting expedition ended in a complete disaster at the Battle of Río Bueno. This setback did not stop the Spanish who under the leadership of Salazar organized a new expedition the summer of 1655." It then has the Mapuche rising as that expedition was being prepared — "As the slave raiding expedition of 1655 was being prepared indios amigos begun to express unease" — and Salazar beginning his campaign on 6 February with the attacks following on 14 February. Precondition-of and not caused: the article is explicit that the defeat did not stop the raiding, so the battle is a step on the way to the expedition the rising answered and not the thing that brought the rising about.
